description: NEGATIVE (issue #825): deferredness reaches the WHOLE enclosing chain, not one level. The `every` handler is registered inside a `repeat` body — an eager scope — so a checker that only re-based its immediate parent would still resolve the root through the eager, position-limited view and report `:label` as undefined. It must not: `spec/execution-model.md:617-637` makes a handler capture the scope it was registered in, and that scope outlives the loop turn, so the handler COULD fire after line 2 — which is all `spec/execution-model.md:423-424` needs, since the checker may not report a name a deferred handler could reach. Note what the run stage does and does not show here: this program has no `wait`, so under the harness's empty host the handler never actually fires and `execute()` being clean is not evidence either way. The claim this fixture pins is the CHECK stage. This is the case that rules out the one-level version of the eager/deferred split, and it was named as a trap during #825's review gate before the two-chain model existed; a mutation that limits deferredness to one level fails this fixture and no other.
